transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02 14:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Meeting ID: ff-2026-12-02-oxfordshore-ctrlplane-5821
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Lena (CISO, Oxford Shore), Tom (Head of Platform), Priya (Privacy Counsel), Marcus (SRE)

[00:00] Ava Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining we got about 50 minutes today, quick intros then jump into the control plane and logging questions you sent over in the form.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz: great, thanks. i'll be quick i'm lena ciso, priya is our privacy counsel, tom runs platform and marcus is our sre. main ask is we need to understand where PII might live, how logs are retained and what controls map to our auditors for 2027.
[00:28] Samir Patel: perfect thanks lena. just to confirm, are you mostly evaluating hosted redwood api or are you already leaning toward Dedicated/private?
[00:35] Tom Reynolds: we're honestly open but leaning away from plain hosted. primary concerns are log retention, key residency, and separation of control plane so the legal team can argue minimal exposure.
[00:47] Priya Kaur: and for clarity we have EU customers; GDPR is a hard requirement. secondarily we have a line of business that handles health-adjacent data — not full HIPAA but could touch PHI-like fields — so we need to know if the platform can be put inside our VPC or if logs can be scrubbed prior to export.
[01:05] Samir Patel: that's helpful. high-level: Redwood Hosted has a hardened control plane with SOC 2; Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and stronger isolation; Private (VPC/on-prem) gives the maximum control - both for KMS/BYOK and network egress. but there are tradeoffs re: ops burden and cost.
[01:25] Marcus Vale: can you be specific about logs? what do you keep by default, how long, and can we control that per route or ingestion?
[01:33] Samir Patel: default hosted retention is 30 days for request/response telemetry and 90 days for certain operational metrics, with access controls. with Dedicated we can shorten retention or disable request body retention; Private gives you total control since logs stay in your infra. note that some system logs for debugging are necessary for SLA investigations and we recommend configurable redaction.
[01:51] Lena Ortiz: when you say "disable request body retention" does that mean you still keep request metadata (timestamps, token counts) or is that purged as well?
[01:59] Samir Patel: metadata like timestamps, model id, token counts are typically retained for billing/SLOs. request/response content containing PII can be redacted automatically by a configured scrubber before it's written to persistent logs. that scrubber can run regex rules and also an ML-based PII classifier.
[02:15] Tom Reynolds: is the scrubber on the control plane or data plane? i.e., does the content leave our network unredacted during evaluation in hosted mode?
[02:22] Samir Patel: in hosted default the data flows through Redwood's data plane and the scrubber sits there — it's applied prior to long-term storage, but there is a short-lived transit window. for customers with strict residency concerns we recommend Dedicated with our private VPC peering or Private deployment where the data plane is inside your VPC and the control plane remains minimal and only metadata is exchanged.
[02:46] Priya Kaur: hmm that transit window is a regulatory concern. what options do you have for control-plane separation? can the control plane be hosted in a different region or be limited to metadata only?
[02:56] Samir Patel: yes, a common pattern is to run the control plane in Redwood's hosted region while the data plane and inference engines run in Dedicated nodes that sit in customer VPCs; only health/telemetry roll-ups are sent and we can configure telemetry to be synthetic metrics only. for strict customers we support region-locking and can disable user request payloads from being sent to the control plane.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: what about BYOK for keys? auditors will want KMS or HSM with customer-managed keys.
[03:27] Samir Patel: we support BYOK for Dedicated and Private. you can either bring keys via supported cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK) or we can integrate with an HSM for on-prem. Hosted customers can use Redwood-managed keys, but we also offer envelope encryption with a customer rotation plan — though it's not identical to full BYOK.
[03:46] Marcus Vale: and syslog export? we need to forward logs to our SIEM and also keep raw request headers for incident response — can that be done without including request bodies?
[03:56] Jordan Lee: yes, we've got syslog/elk/s3 forwarding. you can export structured logs with fields you choose; many customers export metadata and audit trails to SIEM while keeping bodies in a separate, encrypted blob store or disabling them entirely. we can set up a pipeline during the pilot to validate the fields.
[04:15] Priya Kaur: in the event of a DSAR (data subject access request) — can we delete request bodies on demand? what's the deletion SLA?
[04:24] Samir Patel: deletion APIs exist and can be run against stored request bodies. for Hosted it's a 48 hour window to remove artifacts from persistent stores, though some backup snapshots can be longer — we provide attestations. Dedicated/private deletion timelines are configurable and usually faster since it's under customer's control.
[04:41] Tom Reynolds: auditors also ask about chain of custody and audit logs for admin actions. do you log admin UI/API actions and do customers get the raw audit trail?
[04:50] Samir Patel: yes, admin actions are logged; we can provide read-only audit exports with user ids, timestamps, IPs for retention periods you choose. for private installs you keep the audit trail locally.
[05:02] Lena Ortiz: okay a few corner cases: subsidiary data transfers — we have EEA->US processing for billing. can Redwood help regionize processing so that EEA traffic never leaves EU data centers?
[05:13] Samir Patel: yes region-locking is supported; you can pin models and inference nodes to specific regions. our routing rules will keep requests in region and failover to another region only if you opt into cross-region fallback.
[05:24] Marcus Vale: about logs we saw in your docs mention of kv cache and token prefetch metrics, are those considered PII? we have a prompt bank that contains customer names in prompts.
[05:34] Jordan Lee: KV cache entries are ephemeral and not normally persisted to long-term logs; but if prompts are stored for debugging they need redaction. recommend enabling prefix/KV caching but turning off prompt retention unless you have pilot acceptance.
[05:46] Tom Reynolds: what about encryption in transit and at rest? auditors want AES-256 at rest and TLS1.2+ in transit.
[05:54] Samir Patel: we use TLS1.2+ for transport and AES-256 for at-rest encryption. Dedicated and Private can be configured to use your CMEK keys.
[06:03] Priya Kaur: wondering about subpoenas and legal process: who has access to keys? if we bring our own key does Redwood have any technical ability to decrypt?
[06:12] Samir Patel: with BYOK store the key in your KMS and Redwood never has the plaintext key. we only get a wrapped key for operations. so decryption would require the KMS account to grant access — that reduces the risk of third-party subpoena access.
[06:27] Lena Ortiz: great. cost question: locking to EU region or Dedicated raises costs. can you give a sense of incremental price and the service-levels?
[06:34] Ava Martinez: yes i can follow up with a Dedicated pricing sheet; short answer is Dedicated has a monthly reserved commit plus lower per-token unit cost; region locking may add infra overhead but we'll include those numbers in the sheet we send.
[06:47] Tom Reynolds: we also need to know about data portability if we decide to leave — are there export bundles and do you keep a copy?
[06:55] Jordan Lee: we provide export bundles for customers, including request/response bodies if retained, and an activation of deletion upon export. We keep operational backups for 30 days and provide attestations for sanitized copies.
[07:08] Priya Kaur: small but important: do you support SAML/SSO with SCIM provisioning and role-based access controls so we can tie into our IdP?
[07:15] Samir Patel: yes SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC are supported across Hosted, Dedicated, Private with enterprise plans.
[07:23] Marcus Vale: one more from ops — rate limiting and burst protection. if we run a steady batch workload (large embeddings), can we isolate that to avoid noisy-neighbor impact?
[07:33] Samir Patel: Dedicated gives you reserved GPUs and isolation; for Hosted we do soft isolation and QoS rules; you can configure per-route limits and separate model instances. Also Redwood Optimize can recommend batching for embeddings to reduce unit cost.
[07:51] Lena Ortiz: what about evidence for auditors: does Redwood provide encryption attestations, pen test results, SOC2 PDF etc?
[07:58] Ava Martinez: yes we'll send the SOC2 Type II report, our penetration test summary (redacted), and HIPAA attestation for customers with a BA agreement.
[08:08] Tom Reynolds: can we get a proof-of-concept that simulates our worst-case latency and token volume — and also checks that syslog export doesn't include bodies?
[08:16] Samir Patel: absolutely. propose a 2-week pilot: we deploy Dedicated nodes in your EU region (or Private in your VPC if you prefer), run synthetic traffic matching peak QPS, validate tail-latency and token costs, and run the syslog export validation.
[08:31] Priya Kaur: pilot acceptance criteria should include no transit of unredacted PII off EU infra, delete-on-demand within 48 hours, and audit logs for admin actions.
[08:42] Ava Martinez: noted, we'll include those as acceptance criteria in the pilot doc.
[08:48] Marcus Vale: small nit: what happens with model rollout changes, e.g., if you upgrade a model and it changes tokenization, how do we validate regression?
[08:56] Jordan Lee: we support pinned model versions and can do canary rollouts. Redwood Console will show token delta and quality regressions; for Dedicated we avoid automatic upgrades unless you opt in.
[09:09] Lena Ortiz: ok last items — compliance flow: privacy counsel will review BAAs and DPA language. Priya will send redlines.
[09:18] Priya Kaur: yes i'll send redlines and a brief list of mandatory clauses: data residency guarantees, right to delete, auditability, key control.
[09:28] Ava Martinez: perfect. quick recap and next steps: we'll send SOC2/HIPAA docs, Dedicated pricing, VPC architecture diagram, and propose pilot dates. we'll also set up a technical deep-dive with Samir and Marcus to walk through syslog export and redaction rules.
[09:44] Tom Reynolds: sounds good, thanks.
[09:47] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[09:50] [Meeting ends]

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker labels may have overlapped, some technical terms transcribed as 'k-v cache' or 'kv cash' in the raw transcript. references: pricing sheet (link shared in chat), SOC2/HIPAA artifacts (to be emailed).
